task.title: Keep --all-elements discovery and --fetch-sources cheap on large projects
task.problem: On a large project, -ar --fetch-sources grew memory with every link and subproject and ran slowly: listing targets loaded a full element graph (elements, sources and source keys) once per subproject batch and once per link, and --fetch-sources loaded the selection again before the search load.
task.proposal: List targets with BuildStream's Loader only (kind and full name, links resolved) without instantiating elements, bisect failing batches, and fetch from the same loaded elements that are searched.
acceptance: Target discovery for --all-elements/--include-subprojects instantiates no elements; a failing batch is bisected to the broken recipes.
--fetch-sources loads the selection once per option set and searches those elements.
Results, diagnostics and exit statuses of the existing --all-elements and --fetch-sources tests are unchanged.
evidence: Synthetic project with 4 x 1000 elements (local sources) and 200 links, -ar --find --fetch-sources, BuildStream 2.8.1: 248 s / 700 MB max RSS before, 40 s / 152 MB after (cold cache); 27 s warm.
test_element_targets_read_recipes_without_instantiating_elements and the junction integration test pass.
